key_concepts: Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of molecules
Molecules are constantly moving and have kinetic energy
Faster molecular motion corresponds to higher temperature
Heat is energy transferred from higher to lower temperature bodies
Heat and temperature are related but not the same
Heat transfer occurs through conduction, convection, and radiation
Conductivity and temperature difference affect heat transfer rate
Senses are unreliable for measuring temperature; thermometers are used
Liquid-in-glass thermometers contain mercury that expands or contracts with temperature ch
Water boils at 100°C and temperature remains constant during boiling
Thermal expansion involves particles spreading out; contraction involves decreased average
Mechanical equivalent of heat is 4.186 J per calorie
